name: Polycab India Ltd
title: Polycab India Ltd - 542652 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Polycab Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 27% YoY with EBITDA margin at 13.1% and record quarterly PAT of INR 7.9 bn, while Cable & Wire volumes grew only low single digits.
summary.overview: Management reported record annual and quarterly revenue, with Q4 consolidated revenue up 27% YoY and PAT of INR 7.9 bn (up 7%, 8.9% margin). Growth was price-led: cumulative price hikes of 18-19% were taken from January to March, while Cable & Wire volumes grew low single digits in the quarter. Middle East escalation, PVC price spikes and pollution-related construction halts hit March, which is the key month of Q4. FY26 was a record year: revenue above INR 285 bn (+29%), EBITDA margin 13.9%, PAT above INR 27 bn (+32%), and FY26 volume growth of 18%.

segments.name: Wires & Cables
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 30% YoY, with domestic cables up 30% and combined volume growth in low single digits. EBIT margin was 13.1%, and Q4 EBITDA margin was around 14%+. Cables outpaced wires, and institutional sales grew faster than channel.

segments.name: FMEG
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 47% YoY, the ninth straight quarter of outperformance versus industry. EBIT margin was 4.1%, and FY26 EBITDA margin was mid-single digit. Solar was the largest FMEG category, growing 2x; premium fans were about 25% and premium lighting about 35% of segment revenue.

segments.name: International (exports)
segments.commentary: Grew 18% YoY and contributed 4.4% of consolidated revenue in Q4. Full-year export share was 5.4%, and Middle East was about 16% of FY26 exports, which was hit during the quarter.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue fell 15% YoY to INR 5,098 mn on project execution timing. Segment profit was INR 386 mn, a 7.6% margin. Sustainable margin is guided at mid to high single digits.

guidance_outlook: Project Spring: Cables & Wires to grow at 1.5x industry growth; FMEG at 1.5x-2x industry growth.
Near to mid-term EBITDA margin guided at 12-14%; long-term 11-13%.
Exports to reach more than 10% of revenue by FY30; management expects exports to grow beyond 5% in FY27 and hopes to get there sooner.
Working capital cycle expected to revert to 45-50 days from 25 days in Q4.
Dividend payout to exceed 30% by FY30 (27.2% in FY26).
Capex of INR 60-80 bn over 5 years; FY27 capex guided at INR 12-16 bn per year; FY30 capex of INR 60-80 bn cited as Project Spring target.
EHV capacity expected on stream by end of calendar 2026, with revenue contribution from FY28.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation is mid-70s (75-76%); management says plants practically reach early 90s but a sustainable level is 80-85%.
FY26 capex was about INR 14.8 bn, including roughly INR 15 bn invested in capacity expansion; the company plans INR 1.2-1.6 bn of capacity addition every year.
Around 90% of capex goes to Cable & Wire capacity (largely fungible), about 5% to backward integration and 3-4% to FMEG.
EHV (extra high voltage) capacity is on track to be commissioned by end of calendar 2026; about 50% of domestic EHV consumption is imported.
Management says there will be no scenario where Polycab runs out of capacity over the next 4-5 years.
demand_pricing: Cumulative price hikes of about 18-19% were taken from January to March; pass-through of copper, aluminium and PVC is described as complete and in tandem with input costs.
Volume growth was low single digits in Q4 as West Asia tensions, pollution-related construction halts and PVC price spikes (60-80% in early March) hit primary and secondary sales.
FY26 Cable & Wire volume growth was 18%, versus industry growth of 11-12%, with domestic wires and cable organised market share at 30-31% (up 300-400 bps over FY25's 26-27%).
Channel is about 90% of business and institutional about 10%; channel margins are 3-4% higher than institutional. Institutional mix was 2-3 points higher in Q4.
Demand sectors: power 40-45% of cables, manufacturing and private industry 35-40%, mobility 10-12%, energy and exploration 5-6%.
Power capacity additions in FY26 were about 55-56 GW, nearly double FY25; management expects demand to defer by weeks, not be lost.

qa_highlights.question: What were the Cable & Wire volume growth and price hikes taken from January?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined volume growth was low single digits, with cables ahead of wires. Cumulative price hikes were about 18-19% from January to March.

qa_highlights.question: What was the impact of the Middle East disruption in March?
qa_highlights.answer: Primary sales were hit as distributors lifted less, since secondary sales did not move at the expected pace. Private sector demand was hit by gas rationing, and PVC prices rose 60-80% in early March. The impact was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Institutional mix and margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Institutional sales were about 2-3 points higher than channel in Q4 (about 13-14% of the Cable & Wire top line in Q4 per management's arithmetic). Channel margins are 3-4% higher.

qa_highlights.question: Peak utilisation and capacity headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 75-76%. Management says early 90s has been reached at times, but 80-85% is the sustainable level, and there is room for growth.

qa_highlights.question: Use of surplus cash and M&A?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus remains on capex funded from internal accruals and on the dividend payout. M&A is being evaluated in India and abroad, but nothing is in view for the near to mid term.

qa_highlights.question: Export outlook for FY27 and the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a firm number, but expects exports to exceed the current 5.4% share. US distribution was re-established and North America was about 40% of FY26 exports. Middle East was about 15-16% of FY26 exports and is not expected to contribute meaningfully in the near term.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory gains and raw material hedging?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says there are no inventory gains or losses because raw materials are hedged for copper and aluminium, and copper is largely imported. XLPE and compound availability is comfortable for about one quarter, with a diversified vendor base.

qa_highlights.question: Segment EBITDA margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Cable & Wire Q4 EBITDA margin was around 14%+, and above the 13.9% company level for FY26. FMEG was mid-single digit for both Q4 and FY26.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict, Brent around USD 100/bbl and a record-low rupee (INR 94.83/USD) raise input and inflation risk; the company's stated pass-through has so far held.
Working capital at 25 days in Q4 is flattered by letter-of-credit payables; reversion to 45-50 days would absorb cash.
Institutional mix rising reduces margins (channel is 3-4% higher); watch the mix next quarter.
March volume shortfall: whether primary sales recover as secondary sales normalise, and whether stocking unwinds.
FMEG margins (EBIT 4.1%) remain well below the 8-10% EBITDA target for FY30; watch the trajectory.
Export share fell to 4.4% in Q4; Middle East recovery timing and the US distribution ramp are open questions.
EHV commissioning by end of calendar 2026 and first revenue in FY28.
summary.management_tone: Confident on structural demand and market share gains, but clearly cautious on the near term: management acknowledged March softness and volume growth in low single digits. Answers on volume split and inventory gains were brief, and the company declined to give a firm FY27 export or growth number.
key_quotes: Importantly, these gains are not cyclical but very much structural in nature, driven by a shift towards organized players, increasing preference for quality and compliance and our ability to serve customers reliably across geographies.
So we have a hedging mechanism in place. So we don't have any inventory gain unlike peers.
So whatever we've delivered is again the best side of the industry growth.
So in FY28, you'll be able to see revenues from EHV.

adds.what: Ongoing Cable & Wire capacity additions of INR 1.2-1.6 bn per year

growth.why: Management guides to Cable & Wire growing 1.5x industry and FMEG 1.5-2x industry under Project Spring, backed by INR 60-80 bn five-year capex, mid-70s utilisation (75-76%) and EHV capacity due by end-CY2026, but no explicit numeric revenue growth guide for FY27 was given and Q4 volume growth was only low single digits.
